h:
Enums are not a built-in Luau type and they exist only in Roblox, but they're conceptually similar to other Luau data types and are something you'll work with frequently in Roblox development.

The enumeration data type, or Enum, is a fixed list of items. You can access enums through the global object called Enum. For a full list and their respective items, see Enums.

Enum items

To get all items of an enum, call the GetEnumItems() method on it. The following code sample demonstrates how to call GetEnumItems() on the PartType enum.

local partTypes = Enum.PartType:GetEnumItems()

for index, enumItem in partTypes do
    print(enumItem)
end

--[[
    Enum.PartType.Ball
    Enum.PartType.Block
    Enum.PartType.Cylinder
    Enum.PartType.Wedge
    Enum.PartType.CornerWedge
]]

Data type

The EnumItem is the data type for items in enums. An EnumItem has three properties:

  • Name — The name of the EnumItem.
  • Value — The numerical index of the EnumItem.
  • EnumType — The parent Enum of the EnumItem.

Some properties of objects can only be items of certain enums. For example, the Shape property of a Part object is an item of the PartType enum. The following code sample demonstrates how to print the properties of the PartType.Cylinder enum item.

print(Enum.PartType.Cylinder.Name) --> "Cylinder"
print(Enum.PartType.Cylinder.Value) --> 2
print(Enum.PartType.Cylinder.EnumType) --> PartType

To assign an EnumItem as the value of a property, use the full Enum declaration. You can also use the item's Name property as a string.

local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local part = Instance.new("Part") -- Create a new part

part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder -- By full enum item declaration (best practice)
part.Shape = "Cylinder" -- By enum item's name as a string

part.Parent = Workspace

kid.simple: An enum is a fixed list of choices that Roblox gives you, like all the shapes a part can be: Ball, Block, Cylinder, and so on. You use enums to set properties without typos, like `part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Ball`. Each choice is called an enum item, and it has a name, a number value, and the enum it belongs to.
kid.analogy: An enum is like a menu with a few fixed options. You cannot order something that is not on the menu, and each item has a name and a number next to it.
keyPoints: An enum is a fixed list of items. You reach them all through the global `Enum`.
Enums only exist in Roblox; they are not a built-in Luau type.
`Enum.PartType:GetEnumItems()` gives you a list of every item in that enum.
Each `EnumItem` has `Name` (like "Cylinder"), `Value` (a number, like 2), and `EnumType` (the enum it belongs to, like `PartType`).
Some properties only accept items from one enum. A part's `Shape` uses `Enum.PartType`.
Best practice: set properties with the full enum, like `part.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder`.
You can also use the item's name as a string, like `part.Shape = "Cylinder"`, but the full enum is safer.

terms.enum (enumeration): A fixed list of named choices, like `Enum.PartType` with Ball, Block, Cylinder, Wedge, and CornerWedge.
terms.EnumItem: One choice from an enum, like `Enum.PartType.Cylinder`.
terms.Name: The item's name as text. `Enum.PartType.Cylinder.Name` is "Cylinder".
terms.EnumType: The enum an item belongs to. For `Enum.PartType.Cylinder`, it is `PartType`.
terms.global: Available everywhere without needing to get it first. `Enum` is a global.

example.title: Make a part with a random shape
example.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

-- Get every shape a part can be
local shapes = Enum.PartType:GetEnumItems()
for _, item in shapes do
	print(item.Name, item.Value)
end

-- Pick one at random
local randomShape = shapes[math.random(1, #shapes)]

local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Shape = randomShape -- set the property with an EnumItem
part.Anchored = true
part.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
part.Parent = Workspace

print("Made a", randomShape.Name)
explain: `GetEnumItems()` returns a table of all the part shapes.
The loop prints each shape's name and number value.
`math.random(1, #shapes)` picks a random position in the list.
The new part's `Shape` is set to that EnumItem, and the part is placed in Workspace.

watchOut: Misspelling the string, like `part.Shape = "Cylender"`. Use `Enum.PartType.Cylinder` so Studio can catch typos.
Using an item from the wrong enum. `Shape` needs a `PartType` item, not a `Material` item.
